blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team swaps a working three-step chain for a framework that hides the prompts, and debugging gets harder. Which advice from the article applies?

options.text: Keep the framework, and add a second one to watch it
options.says: Ruled out because frameworks "often create extra layers of abstraction that can obscure the underlying prompts and responses, making them harder to debug".

options.text: Return to direct LLM API calls, and read any code beneath
options.says: The first page says "We suggest that developers start by using LLM APIs directly", and to understand the code under any framework.

options.text: Move the sequence into an agent so that the model finds the path
options.says: Ruled out because agents are for "open-ended problems where it's difficult or impossible to predict the required number of steps", and a fixed sequence is not one.

options.text: Wrap the framework in one more layer that logs each call
options.says: Ruled out because the article says "don't hesitate to reduce abstraction layers and build with basic components as you move to production", not to add one.

questions.stem: A classifier's output comes back as `REFUNDS.`, with capitals and a full stop, but the program's table is keyed by lowercase names. What should the program do before the table lookup?

options.text: Normalize the text into a form that matches a known route
options.says: The first page says "The program normalizes the label, looks it up, and sends anything unknown to a default route."

options.text: Retry the classifier until an output matches a name exactly
options.says: Ruled out because the page sends "anything unknown to a default route" and describes no second call to the classifier.

options.text: Send the output to the default route without a lookup
options.says: Ruled out because the program "normalizes the label, looks it up", so a reply that matches after cleaning is not sent straight to the default.

options.text: Hand the output to a person who picks the route
options.says: Ruled out because "The failure to design for is a label that matches no route.", and the program meets it with a default and not with a person.

questions.stem: A code review sends one snippet to the model three times in parallel and applies a threshold to the answers. Which variation is this?

options.text: Sectioning, where independent subtasks run side by side
options.says: Ruled out because sectioning is "Breaking a task into independent subtasks run in parallel", and here one task is repeated.

options.text: Chaining, where each call processes the output of an earlier one
options.says: Ruled out because chaining is for steps "where each LLM call processes the output of the previous one", and these runs do not depend on each other.

options.text: Routing, where a classifier picks a specialized followup
options.says: Ruled out because "Routing classifies an input and directs it to a specialized followup task", and here nothing is classified.

options.text: Voting, where repeated runs of one task are counted
options.says: The first page defines voting as "Running the same task multiple times to get diverse outputs", and says "a vote is a count and a threshold".

questions.stem: A fan-out workflow plans three subtasks and one worker throws an exception. What does the practice's orchestrator do?

options.text: Stops the run and reports a failure, since a missing result makes the answer unsafe
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "one failure must not stop the others".

options.text: Retries the failed worker until it succeeds, and then combines all three
options.says: Ruled out because "A worker can fail, and one failure must not stop the others", and the page describes no retry.

options.text: Marks it failed, runs the others, and reports a partial answer
options.says: The second page says one failure must not stop the others, "the subtask is marked failed and the rest run", and a partial result is reported as partial.

options.text: Drops the failed subtask without a trace and combines the other two as if complete
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "A partial result is reported as partial", so the failure is visible.
